symptom: No MDL form bound the pluggable Image widget to an uploaded image (an entity extending System.Image) — mendixlabs/mxcli#1476. In a data view over one, `image i ()` failed "No image selected.", `image i (ImageType: dynamicImage)` passed mxcli check AND mx check while naming no real source, and `dynamicimage` is CE0582 "Widget dynamic image is not supported in React client."
cause: The `image` operation only wrote a collection entry (WidgetValue.Image). An image-typed value also holds the context object, as its EntityRef, and nothing wrote, read or validated that: `Image: $currentObject` parsed as a variable and was refused as MDL-WIDGET42; describe had no form for it; `defaultImageDynamic` had no mapping; MDL-WIDGET22 silently passed any unknown ImageType.
insight: **With no Studio Pro sample, mxbuild's refusals are the evidence a shape is read.** No repo project has a dynamic Image widget (all 47 in pedapp/expr-checker are static), so the EntityRef shape was settled by patching raw BSON and running `mx check`: DirectEntityRef to the context entity -> 0 errors; to System.User -> CE7247 "Entity should be the same as the enclosing"; over a non-image entity -> CE7247 "Widget expects entity of type System.Image." A 0-error result alone could mean an ignored key; the two refusals prove it is read. Then the runtime closed the last gap — `playwright` read the img's naturalWidth (40x30, the exact PNG a Java action stored) — since a bound widget that renders the fallback would also pass every lower check. **The forced-fault control showed a second defect**: stubbing the binding write gave CE0463 BEFORE "No image selected.", because `defaultImageDynamic` is hidden unless imageObject is bound — so `DefaultImage:` beside a collection entry is CE0463 and is now refused. Run controls with --no-update-widgets or CE0463 is normalised away. **Two def.json copies** (sdk/ is the embedded one the registry reads; modelsdk/ mirrors it) — edit both. ImageType unknown values are a WARNING, not error: an existing test pinned 'left alone' for future widget versions; silence was the bug, blocking would be a new one.
